# Vocabulary: risk

Primary risks of using a technique in simulation games.

| id | label | definition |
|---|---|---|
| `consistency` | Consistency / hallucination | Outputs contradict world state or prior outputs. |
| `latency` | Latency | Too slow for the interaction loop. |
| `compute-cost` | Compute cost | Per-player-hour inference or training cost threatens margins. |
| `controllability` | Controllability | Designers cannot reliably constrain or tune behavior. |
| `content-safety` | Content safety | May produce harmful, offensive, or age-inappropriate content. |
| `ip-provenance` | IP / provenance | Training data or output ownership is contested; platform disclosure rules apply. |
| `evaluation` | Evaluation difficulty | Hard to test or QA because output space is open-ended. |
| `player-trust` | Player trust / reception | Players or press may reject AI-generated content. |
| `determinism` | Determinism | Breaks replays, lockstep multiplayer, or bug reproduction. |
| `legibility` | Legibility | Players cannot form a mental model of why the system behaved as it did. |
| `labor` | Labor displacement | Changes or removes creative roles; may face workforce opposition. |
